Email: kianmehr.m@gmail.com; Kianmehr.m@gmu.ac.ir Breast cancer is a complex disease which is found as the second cause of cancerassociated death among women. Accumulating of evidence indicated that various factors (i.e., gentical and envirmental factors) could be associated with initiation and progression of breast cancer. Diagnosis of breast cancer patients in early stages is one of important aspects of breast cancer treatment. Among of various diagnosis platforms, imaging techniques are main diagnosis approaches which could provide valuable data on patients with breast cancer. It has been showed that various imaging techniques such as mammography, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron-emission tomography (PET), Computed tomography (CT), and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) could be used for diagnosis and monitoring patients with breast cancer in various stages. Beside, imaging techniques, utilization of biochemical biomarkers such as proteins, DNAs, mRNAs, and microRNAs could be employed as new diagnosis and therapeutic tools for patients with breast cancer. Here, we summarized various imaging techniques and biochemical biomarkers could be utilized as diagnosis of patients with breast cancer. Moreover, we highlighted microRNAs and exosomes as new diagnosis and therapeutic biomarkers for monitoring patients with breast cancer. Moreover, we highlighted utilization of various biomarkers such as measurement of enzymes, miRNAs, and exosomes as diagnostic and therapeutic biomarkers for patients with breast cancer. 2 | IMAGING TECHNIQUES AND BREAST CANCER Breast cancer is one of important malignancies worldwide which has accounted as the most cancer among women. Early detection and monitoring of patients are found as main aspects of breast cancer therapy (Weigel & Dowsett, 2010). Breast cancer could be diagnosed by monitoring of patients with imaging techniques or symptoms such as pain or a palpable mass. It has been showed; the monitoring healthy subjects could contribute to detection of small tumors which could lead to progression of breast cancer (Weigel & Dowsett, 2010). Among of various techniques, imaging techniques have been emerged as powerful tools for detection and monitoring response to therapy in patients with breast cancer (Table 1) (Alcantara, Leal, GarciaBocanegra, & Garcia-Martin, 2014). Mammography is known as gold standard techniques for detection of breast cancer patients which are associated with various benefits such as high sensitivity and specificity, inexpensive, and well tolerated (Wellings, Vassiliades, & Abdalla, 2016). It has been showed that using of mammography could reduce 19% breast cancer mortality. Besides, various benefits of mammography, there are some limitations which are associated with using this technique such as pain and anxiety, false alarms, and radiation risks (Wellings et al., 2016). Hence, it seems that utilization of new techniques with better properties are needed. Ultrasounds is other major imaging techniques which are known as other most common method for diagnosis and monitoring response to therapy in breast cancer (Ozmen et al., 2015). Ultrasounds is other major imaging techniques which are known as other most common method for diagnosis and monitoring response to therapy in breast cancer (Ozmen et al., 2015). Besides, mammography, using of ultrasound is required for the management and diagnosis of breast pathology (Ozmen et al., 2015). The utilization of ultrasound are associated with various advantages (e.g., it does not use ionizing radiation, and high sensitivity), which have provided it as powerful diagnosis tools for detection of breast tumors in young women and pregnant and breastfeeding women (Alcantara et al., 2014). Ultrasound techniques such including Ultrasound contrast and Elastography are also applied for breast intervention, and for the placement of harpoons (Alcantara et al., 2014). In a study, Jia et al. (2014) assessed breast tumor angiogenesis by three-dimensional contrast enhanced ultrasound (3D-CEUS) and dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) score systems as diagnosis platforms in 35 benign and 148 malignant breast tumors. They results indicated that 3D-CEUS score system could be used as an effective diagnosis plathform for evaluation of tumor angiogenesis in patients with breast cancer. Their results showed that this score system shows a well association with various tumor perfusion and vascular characteristics such as microvessel density (MVD), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2, MMP-9) expression (Jia et al., 2014). MRI is found as other important diagnostic tools for breast cancer. This technique could be used for various aspects of breast cancer treatment including monitoring of response to therapy, monitoring high risk patients, assessment of breast cancer metastasis, and study of tumor recurrence (Mann, Kuhl, Kinkel, & Boetes, 2008). The provided data by MRI, could suggested various actions (e.g., breast discharge, staging of breast cancer, evaluation of microcalcifications, premalignant lesions, and residual tumor in operated patients) to clinicians (Sardanelli et al., 2010). These properties led to introduced MRI as a suitable diagnosis technique for patients with breast cancer (Mann et al., 2008; Sardanelli et al., 2010). The mentioned techniques including mammography, ultrasounds, and MRI could be employed as effective tools for detection and monitoring patients with breast cancer (Alcantara et al., 2014). On the other hands, these techniques are associated with various limitations such as lacks of sensibility. Hence, radiologist has efforted to introduce new techniques which could overcome to the current limitations (Alcantara et al., 2014). It has been showed that utilization of external substances called contrast agents which are able to improve the sensibility of images in the region of interest, could be effective platforms for diagnosis and monitoring patients in early stages of various cancers such as breast cancer (Alcantara et al., 2014). The using of contrast agents could enhance the quality and the follow-up of molecular processes at the cellular and molecular levels of the region under assessment. The gadolinium- and iodine-based structures are known as common contrast agents which could be used for MRI and mammography (X-ray), respectively (Alcantara et al., 2014). SPECT technique uses isotopes which emit gamma photons, including 99mTc, 123I, or 125I (Benard & Turcotte, 2005). In a study, Uematsu et al. (2005) assessed the efficacy of PET and SPECT imaging techniques in 15 patients with bone metastases of breast cancer. They results indicated that the sensitivity for diagnosing bone metastases was 85% for SPECT and 17% for PET, specificity of SPECT and PET were 99% and 100%, and accuracy were 96% and 85%, respectively. They revealed that SPECT was classified the bone metastases as 92% of metastases as osteoblastic and 35% of metastases as osteolytic, whereas PET was classified 6% of metastases as osteoblastic and 90% of metastases as osteolytic. These findings suggested that SPECT and PET could be used for diagnosis breast cancer patients with bone metastasis (Uematsu et al., 2005). Multiple lines of evidence indicated that imaging techniques could provide effective information on breast tumor morphology and functional and metabolic processes within the tumor at various levels (Alcantara et al., 2014). It has been showed that the sensitivity of the various imaging techniques is varied depending on the type of biomarkers applied in signaling the vital processes. These studies suggested that imaging techniques could be employed for diagnosis and monitoring response to therapy in patients with breast cancer (Alcantara et al., 2014). 3 | BIOCHEMICAL MARKERS AND BREAST CANCER The utilization of various imaging techniques is associated with several limitations such as expensive, lack of sensitivity, specificity (Alcantara et al., 2014). Hence, it seems that introducing new biomarkers which could overcome to the related limitations of imaging techniques are required. The employing of various biomarkers is known as one of important aspects of diagnosis and monitoring patients with breast cancer (Duffy et al., 2017). The suitable biomarkers could contribute to better understanding of cellular and molecular pathways involved in breast cancer pathogenesis (Duffy et al., 2017). These findings could help to designing effective therapeutic approach and monitoring response to treatment in patients with breast cancer. Several studies indicated that a variety of biochemical biomarkers including proteins (i.e., Her2, ER, and Ki67), mRNAs (i.e., ER α,E Rβ, and ERR γ), enzymes (i.e., CEA and TSGF), and microRNAs (i.e., miR-21, miR-10b, miR-155, and miR-145) could be used as diagnostic biomarkers for detection and monitoring breast cancer patients (Duffy et al., 2017; Kurozumi et al., 2017) (Table 2). The human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is one of important proteins involved in breast cancer pathogenesis (Iqbal, 2014). HER2 is found as a member of the epidermal growth factor receptor family which has tyrosine kinase activity (Schrohl, Pedersen, Jensen, Nielsen, & Brunner, 2011). This receptor could be involved in the regulation of cell growth, survival, and differentiation via targeting multiple signal transduction pathways. It has been showed that dimerization of the receptor could lead to auto-phosphorylation of tyrosine residues within the cytoplasmic domain of the receptors (Iqbal, 2014). In a study, Soliman and Yussif (2016a) assessed the utilization of Ki-67 as prognostic and diagnostic biomarkers for monitoring 107 patients with breast cancer. They also investigated the estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2 in patients with breast cancer. Their results indicated that 44, 23, 15, and 25 subjects were classified as luminal A, luminal B, HER2 subtype, and triple-negative (TN), respectively. They showed that in No luminal A patients levels of Ki-67 were higher than 15%, and their recurrence was 20%. In luminal B group, Ki-67 levels were higher than 15% and recurrence was 39% in 69% of patients. In HER2 subtype, in 34% of cases, Ki-67 levels were higher than 15% and recurrence was 40%. Finally, in triple-negative subjects, in 60% of cases, Ki-67 levels were higher than 15%, and recurrence was observed in 32% of patients. These findings suggested that levels of Ki-67 could be applied as predictive biomarkers for monitoring patients with breast cancer (Soliman & Yussif, 2016a). Besides HER2, estrogen receptor (ER), and progesterone receptor (PR) could be used for classification of breast tumor subtyping (Dai, Xiang, Li, & Bai, 2016). The steroid hormone, estradiol, have critical roles in the initiation and progression of breast cancer. It has been showed that various breast cancers could start out as estrogen dependent and express the ER (Dai et al., 2016). Among of various subtypes of ER, ER α is known as main ER subtypes in the mammary epithelium which has important tasks in mammary gland biology and in progression of breast cancer (Li et al., 2010). The following binding of estrogen to ER α, the ligand-activated ER α could be translocated to the nucleus and bind to the responsive element in the promoter. These actions via promoting gene transcription could be associated with stating of a variety of cellular and molecular pathways involved in the progression of breast cancer (McDonnell & Norris, 2002). Multiple lines of evidence indicated that estrogen and ER could contribute to metastasis of breast cancer. Estrogen signaling could affect on epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and ER α signaling has interaction with various EMT regulators such as Snail and Slug (Saha Roy & Vadlamudi, 2012). ER α c o u l db i n dt o the promoter of metastasis tumor antigen (MTA) 3 which could inhibit Snail. Snail is known as a gene which could affect on EMT transition (Fujita et al., 2003). ER α are able to regulation of Slug transcription via making of a co-repressor complex including HDAC1 (histone deacetylase 1) and N-CoR (nuclear receptor co-repressor) (Ye et al., 2008). Evolving evidence indicated that up regulation of ER β could decrease cell proliferation and it could be had anti-proliferative (tumor suppressor) functions (Speirs et al., 2004; Strom et al., 2004). Evolving evidence indicated that up regulation of ER β could decrease cell proliferation and it could be had anti-proliferative (tumor suppressor) functions (Speirs et al., 2004; Strom et al., 2004). Down regulation of ER β was observed in metastatic breast cancer, and up regulation of ER β expression could be related with less metastatic condition and proliferating tumors (Jarvinen, PeltoHuikko, Holli, & Isola, 2000; Skliris et al., 2003). Table 2 listed various predictive biomarkers for detection and monitoring patients with breast cancer. 4 | MIcroRNAs AND EXOSOMES AS DIAGNOSTIC BIOMARKERS FOR BREAST CANCER MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are known as small non-coding RNAs that involved in the regulation of the various target genes at the posttranscriptional phase (Fathullahzadeh, Mirzaei, Honardoost, Sahebkar, & Salehi, 2016; Golabchi et al., 2017; Masoudi, Mehrabian, & Mirzaei, 2017; Mirzaei, Masoudifar, et al., 2017; Simonian, Mosallayi, & Mirzaei, 2017). These molecules act as epigenetic regulators and play critical roles in various biological processes such as development, angiogenesis, growth and differentiation (Hashemi Goradel et al., 2017; Mashreghi et al., 2017; Mirzaei et al., 2016; Rabieian et al., 2017; Rashidi, Malekzadeh, Goodarzi, Masoudifar, & Mirzaei, 2017). It has been showed that deregulation of miRNAs are related with initiation and progression of various diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular, stroke, and diabetes (Hoseini et al., 2017; Mirzaei, 2017; Mirzaei, Ferns, Avan, & Mobarhan, 2017; Mirzaei, Momeni, et al., 2017; Mohammadi, Goodarzi, Jaafari, Mirzaei, & Mirzaei, 2016). Evolving evidence indicated that miRNAs via targeting a variety of cellular and molecular pathways could be involved in breast cancer pathogenesis (Kurozumi et al., 2017).
